_comment: Balance numbers. Never hardcode any of these in logic (CLAUDE.md rule 5). Enemy vision radii and speeds are in data/enemies.json; the detection and alert numbers are here.
_actionPoints: Raised by one from the 2/3/2 of SPEC.md §5's first draft. Hedgerow costs 2 and is the safe artery of §8, so a 2 AP sapper spent his whole turn on a single hedgerow hex and the middle approach was unusable. The scout keeps his +1 over the other roles, which is how §5 stated his edge. Doubling instead would have let a scout cross a third of the map in one turn and taken the pressure out of the 20-turn clock.
_minimumStep: A unit at FULL action points may always move one hex, even into terrain that costs more than its whole pool, spending everything it has. Unused AP is still never banked (SPEC.md §4). This was added when a 2 AP sapper could never enter a 3 AP marsh at all; the pools below now cover that directly, so its remaining job is the wounded trooper of SPEC.md §5, who drops to 1 AP and would otherwise be unable to leave a hedgerow.
_command: The leader's command radius. At the start of each turn a trooper within `radius` hexes of a trooper flagged `leader` in roster.json gets `bonusActionPoints` added to his pool for that turn — he has been given orders. Measured at the moment the pool is filled, so moving next to the leader mid-turn pays off on the following turn. This is a rule, not a trait: it modifies other troopers, and SPEC.md §5's hooks only ever modify their own owner.
_bases: The base values the trait hooks modify (SPEC.md §5, §7, §9). They landed at M3 so every trait can be shown firing against a real number; the systems that act on them — charges and fuses at M5, gunfire at M4/M5, the drop at M6, trooper vision at M4 — arrive later and must read them from here.
_objectives: SPEC.md §7, by kind; data/map.json places them. `chargesNeeded` charges must go off on it to destroy it, in one fuse phase or several. `blastRadius` is in hexes from each charge that goes off: a trooper inside it dies. `alert` is what one explosion on it raises (charges on one objective going off in the same fuse phase are one explosion), heard as noise.explosion. `cutLine`: a scout may destroy it silently instead (actions.cutLine). `destroyedTerrain`: what its hexes become once destroyed, or null to leave them.
_explosionFloor: SPEC.md §6: once anything has exploded, the alert never decays below this state. A cut line is not an explosion.
_scoring: SPEC.md §10. `turnsPerPoint`: one point per this many turns left when the mission ends. `clean` is the bonus for never reaching the `cleanNeverReached` state and never calling the RAF diversion.
_mission: SPEC.md §10. Success needs the primary destroyed and at least `minimumOut` troopers out by the end of the last turn.
_undo: SPEC.md §4 Undo. How many moves or actions of this player phase can be taken back, most recent first; null is every one of them. Never further than the start of the turn, and never across the jump, so nothing the garrison has done is undone. Normal and Hard keep one step, a mis-click net; Easy lets a new player walk the whole turn back (M11b, data/difficulty.json).
_diversion: SPEC.md §4 RAF diversion: once per mission, no AP, while the trooper flagged leader is alive. The alert drops `statesDown` states (never below the explosion floor), every search and held contact is dropped, every trooper is out of contact.
_detection: SPEC.md §6: detection = base(enemy) - cover(terrain) - concealment(trooper) + proximity, then the onDetectionCheck trait hook; spotted when it reaches `threshold`. No dice: the hover readout shows exactly this sum. `cover` is keyed by the cover word in data/terrain.json. `proximity[d]` is the bonus at d hexes, past the end of the list it is 0. A trooper is tested on every hex he entered this turn, or on the hex he stands on if he never moved. Starting numbers, for the M8 balance pass: open ground in an arc is spotted, heavy cover is safe unless an enemy is adjacent, and a scout in heavy cover is safe even then.
_alert: SPEC.md §6. Alert is a points total; `states` are the four dial positions and `from` is the points at which each begins, lowest first. At 0/2/4/7 (SPEC.md §6) one event is not a whole state: one sighting leaves the garrison Calm, and the bridge alone (one explosion, +3) leaves it Suspicious. Points are capped at the last state's `from`. `quietTurnsToDecay` turns with no alert raised drop it to the start of the state below, or to 0 in Calm. `visionBonus` is added to every enemy's vision radius in that state, and `detectionBonus` to every enemy's detection sum: a roused garrison looks harder, not only further. `spotted` is per trooper spotted in a turn, however many enemies saw him, and only when he was not already in contact: a man already counted is not counted again each turn he stays in view. `stone` is a thrown stone, `bodyFound` a body an enemy comes onto or beside and `parachuteFound` an abandoned parachute an enemy comes onto or beside (SPEC.md §9). Enemy fire at troopers raises nothing: the sighting that caused it already counted. `hearingBonus` is added to every noise radius in that state.
_patrols: How the alert states move patrols (SPEC.md §6). Suspicious: a patrol stops to sweep on every `suspiciousPauseEvery`-th turn and walks on the others — read literally, 'pause and sweep' would freeze patrols for the rest of the mission once an explosion pins the alert at Suspicious. A sweep turns the patrol `sweepRotation` hex directions (3 is an about-face). Who reacts to a noise is decided by `noise` below, not by the state. Alarmed: every moving enemy hunts the last known contact; whoever reaches it sweeps, the contact counts as searched, and everyone goes back to their route.
_noise: SPEC.md §6 'the dial is global, the reaction is local'. Every noise happens at a hex and is heard within this many hexes (plus the alert state's hearingBonus), by distance alone: walls do not stop sound. Patrols in earshot walk to it, sweep and go back to their route; sentries cannot leave their post, so they turn to face it for one turn. `found` is a body or a parachute an enemy came onto or beside, on its way or where it ended its go. A sighting is not a noise: the spotters hold their man, and nobody else comes. An explosion is heard from its objective in the enemy phase after it goes off.
_combat: SPEC.md §5 Wounds and §6 contact. A trooper spotted at one detection check and spotted again at the next is shot, at most once per turn. `shotResult` says what a shot does by the cover of the hex he is shot on (light cover hides but does not stop a bullet, M8b): `hit` counts toward `hitsToKill` (the first wounds, the last kills); `pinned` does no harm but takes `pinnedApLoss` off his next pool, never below 1. No dice: the readout shows which it will be. A wounded man's pool is `woundedActionPoints`, with no orders bonus, until he is stabilised; his charges drop on his hex, and a dead man's do too.
_actions: SPEC.md §4 Actions. hide: ends the turn and adds `concealment` on the hex he stops on, until he next spends AP. suppress: gunners only (roles[].suppress), target within his spot radius with a clear line of sight; the target neither fires nor moves on its next go, and is open to a kill until the end of the next player phase. kill: gunners only (roles[].kill), the same visible target as suppress, which must be under suppression and of a killable type (data/enemies.json); one aimed shot from a silenced Sten, raising alert.silenced and heard as noise.silenced (the onFire hook applies, as to gunfire), and it leaves a body. throwStone: a hex up to `range` away, no line of sight needed. stabilise: a full turn, so the helper must not have spent any AP this turn and it costs his whole pool. pickUpCharge: from the hex he stands on. packParachute: his own parachute, from the hex he stands on (SPEC.md §9). placeCharge costs charges.placeApCost through the onPlaceCharge hook. cutLine: scouts only (roles[].cutLine), a full turn on a charge hex of an objective whose kind allows it. swim: a full turn straight across one hex of `across` terrain, not wounded, and, if `requiresDestroyed` names an objective kind, only once one is destroyed; null lets him swim from the start (M11b: while the bridge stood nobody could reach the telephone exchange but over the watched deck, so nobody went for it). A full turn means he has spent no AP yet and it costs his whole pool. passCharge (M11b): hand one charge to a man beside him who can carry it; the giver pays `apCost`, a lot of a 3 AP sapper's turn, the man taking it pays nothing.
_landing: SPEC.md §9 the drop. Each man jumps from his point on the run's flight line (data/map.json dropRuns) and scatters. `scatterWeights[d]` is the weight of scattering exactly d hexes: 1 and 2 are common, 3 is rare, 0 never. The onLand hook's scatterDistance modifies the roll. Among the hexes at that distance, `windWeights` weights each by where it lies from the jump point: within 60 degrees of the wind's direction is downwind, within 60 degrees of against it upwind, the rest across. A man never lands out of play, on the exfil, on impassable ground other than water that wounds (data/terrain.json landing), on another man, or within `enemyClearance` hexes of an enemy; if nowhere at the rolled distance will do, the nearest distance that will. `badLandingTurnsLost` is what a bad landing (wood, marsh) costs, through the onLand hook's landingPenalty.
_spotRadius: SPEC.md §5 gives the scout 3 and is silent on the others; 2 was chosen for sappers and gunners. Its one use is the gunner's suppress (SPEC.md §4): the target must be within it, plus any terrain spotBonus where the gunner stands. There is no fog of war (§6).
_concealment: concealment(trooper) in the detection formula. SPEC.md §5: detection against a scout is reduced one step.
